subject: Clarify: Incident-notify timelines, evidence escrow & subprocessor updates for DPA
messages:
From: Suresh Patel <suresh.patel@datashield.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: procure@globalcloud.com
Date: 2025-08-03T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: DPA: incident notification / evidence escrow questions

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the quick demo yesterday. Procurement asked me to confirm a few specific points in your DPA around incident notification and evidence handling before we move to final legal review. Summary of asks from our side: 

- Notification timeline: the DPA currently references "prompt" notification. Our procurement team needs explicit windows (initial notification + substantial update cadence). We prefer a 48-hour initial notification for incidents that materially affect our data. Can Redwood confirm?
- Scope of notification: does "affected data" include derived telemetry/feature logs? We need clarity so we can assess regulatory impact.
- Evidence & escrow: we need the ability to request a forensics snapshot and a secure handoff/escrow of evidence (time-limited). What is the standard retention you can support for a forensic snapshot and what export formats are available?
- Subprocessors: we'll need a current subprocessor roster and a commitment to 30 days' notice for additions that could impact cross-border transfers (or an update cadence).

I've attached our procurement redlines (DPA_redlines_v1.pdf) with inline comments. Can you route this to the right person on your side (legal/ops) and let us know which items are negotiable vs. policy-driven?

Appreciate it — Suresh

--
Suresh Patel
Head of Procurement, DataShield AI
suresh.patel@datashield.ai

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Suresh Patel <suresh.patel@datashield.ai>

Date: 2025-08-03T13:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: incident notification / evidence escrow questions

Suresh — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marcus (legal/ops) and Naomi (security) so they can respond to the specifics. High-level: we can be prescriptive about timelines and evidence handoff for customers on reserved or enterprise plans; hosted customers have slightly different constraints but we'll call those out.

Next steps from our side:
- Marcus will propose concrete timeline language (initial notification window + follow-up cadence) and an evidence-handover process (what we can provide, format, and retention).
- Naomi will confirm telemetry scope (what we consider "customer data" vs system telemetry) and options for redaction.
- I'll confirm procurement flow for subprocessor roster updates and whether we can commit to a 30-day notice or monthly published list + immediate notification for high-risk additions.

I've attached a short excerpt with the notification section we usually present to enterprise customers (DPA_excerpt_for_notifications.docx). We can iterate.

Will aim to get Marcus's proposed language back to you by end of day tomorrow.

Cheers,

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: Suresh Patel <suresh.patel@datashield.ai>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-08-04T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: incident notification / evidence escrow questions

Suresh — quick read-through and proposed positions below. Inline comments in the attached term sheet (evidence-escrow-term-sheet.pdf). Quoting the main asks and our responses: 

1) Notification timeline
- Your ask: 48-hour initial notice for material incidents.
- Our position: For incidents impacting customer data confidentiality or availability, Redwood can commit to initial notification within 72 hours of detection for Hosted plans. For Dedicated/Private deployments (enterprise customers on reserved capacity or on-prem), we can contractually agree to 48 hours.
- Proposed language: "Redwood will provide initial notification of a Security Incident that materially affects Customer Data within 72 hours of confirmation of the incident. For Dedicated or Private deployments (contracted enterprise plans), Redwood will provide initial notification within 48 hours. Notifications will include a high-level impact summary and next steps; substantive forensic updates will follow as available."

2) Scope of notification (telemetry/derived logs)
- Our definition: "Customer Data" = data ingested by customer requests and any model outputs tied to those requests. System telemetry (metrics, internal debugging logs) is not considered Customer Data unless it contains identifiers or payloads that originated from a Customer.
- Naomi: we can provide an option to include derived telemetry for customers with regulatory requirements, subject to a limited-forensics export and redaction controls.

3) Evidence & escrow
- What we can provide: KV cache snapshots, request/response logs, and a limited forensic snapshot depending on retention window. Format: encrypted archive (.tar.gz) with accompanying manifest (CSV).
- Retention & export window: we propose a standard 90-day secure export window for hosted accounts (shorter for free/trial tiers). For Dedicated/Private customers we can negotiate longer retention.
- Escrow: we don't generally escrow live evidence but will provide a one-off secure handoff via SFTP or encrypted Drive link with audit trail. For heavily regulated customers we can discuss a paid evidence-escrow service.

4) Subprocessors & cross-border changes
- We publish a rolling subprocessor roster monthly. For additions that change cross-border data flows or that are materially high-risk (e.g., new cloud provider in a new jurisdiction), we'll provide notice at least 30 days in advance and offer a mitigation plan.

Open items (we'll need your sign-off):
- Do you require the 48-hour initial notification for Hosted (non-dedicated) as well? If so, we'll need to evaluate operational implications and potential SLA/price adjustments.
- Evidence retention requested (90 days vs 180 days) — please indicate your minimum requirement.
- If DataShield requires escrow as a standing capability rather than a one-off, we can scope a commercial add-on.

Attached: evidence-escrow-term-sheet.pdf (high-level operational notes + redline suggestions). Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Director, Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

From: Suresh Patel <suresh.patel@datashield.ai>

Cc: procure@globalcloud.com
Date: 2025-08-05T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: incident notification / evidence escrow questions

Thanks Marcus — this is helpful and clear. A few quick answers from our side: 

- DataShield requests the 48-hour initial notification for our account (we're on a reserved plan and will be moving to a Dedicated deployment as part of the commercial terms).
- For evidence retention we request a 180-day retention window for forensic snapshots for our Dedicated environment.
- Regarding escrow: we'll accept a one-off secure handoff for now; counsel will flag if they want a standing escrow service later.

If you can update the DPA excerpt with the 48-hour language for Dedicated deployments and note 180-day retention for forensic exports, we can run the revised text through our legal team and aim to sign. Please send DocuSign when ready.

Appreciate the speedy turnaround — Suresh

--
